status: Phase 1 and initial-request consolidation are observed live in user screenshots. Authenticated Server-Timing samples identify database round-trip overhead and expensive connection acquisition. Runtime batching, bounded idle-connection reuse and pool-state diagnostics are implemented locally; deployment and regional-alignment verification pending. Phase 3 overnight orchestration remains planned.

phase2.evidence: User supplied payments-register, student-sync and student-register Server-Timing headers after deployment. Payments uses the new bootstrap endpoint, and Students no longer makes a separate workspace request.
phase2.requires: Deploy the new Runtime round-trip/connection-reuse changes; no frontend update or database migration required for this follow-up.

findings: Normal list endpoints already use tenant-scoped local database records, not live Xero requests.

Students latest-invoice advisor view was repeatedly evaluated for 1068 students. Read-only EXPLAIN ANALYZE: 8768 ms before, 476 ms with a tenant-scoped MATERIALIZED CTE. An earlier baseline was 9177 ms. These are query timings, not end-to-end page timings.
Payments invoice query: 85 ms before, 28 ms after removing a correlated full-sync watermark lookup. Both returned identical first-page rows in the same read-only snapshot.
Invoice sync scheduler runs in the Runtime process when enabled, with a default hourly incremental interval. It can compete with HTTP requests for the same pool and compute.
Sync users currently applies at 02:00 Brisbane, and also queues review scans when invoice sync completes. It skips active invoice sync runs.
Document discovery already runs separately, with durable per-source jobs, leases and retries, but was capped at 25 sources per hour.
No active production contention, API cold-start duration or end-to-end browser latency was proven by this audit. Payments needs correlated timing logs before further changes.
implemented: Compute latest invoice advisors once per student-register request, retaining RLS and existing assignment rules.
Compute the Payments full-sync watermark once using authenticated tenant/connection parameters.

Change document Render cron to 17:00 UTC / 03:00 Brisbane daily. Process at most 500 sources or 30 minutes per invocation, serially, paced 2 seconds apart, stopping on provider backoff. Existing per-source leases and retry state remain authoritative.
Log batch_finished plus remaining status counts; do not imply the entire backlog finished.

Separate queued, processing, failed and completed-empty document UI states. Poll stored metadata every 30 seconds while processing or 120 seconds while queued, for at most 30 visible-page refreshes. Stop on completion/error/navigation/destruction; skip hidden tabs. Keep manual status refresh.

targetArchitecture.interactive: Serve local read models only. Preserve current records while jobs run. Manual Refresh queues durable work; previews/downloads remain available during the day. Show last successful synchronization and degraded status.
targetArchitecture.automaticWindow: 01:00-06:00 Brisbane. Start invoice import at 01:00; perform student linkage and advisor reconciliation after successful import; discover document metadata after linkage. Dependency checkpoints, not just clock offsets, must enforce ordering.
targetArchitecture.workerIsolation: Move invoice and user-sync processing out of HTTP API processes into dedicated workers. Use small separate pools, retain tenant RLS, atomic claims and leases. Disable old scheduler execution only after the replacement worker is proven, without disabling manual enqueue endpoints.
targetArchitecture.consistency: Never mark a source sync successful before its data commits. Resume checkpoints after failures. Keep unmatched invoices Pending action, preserve explicit exclusions and reconcile advisors from the latest dated eligible invoice. Manual daytime imports still need downstream linkage/review reconciliation.
targetArchitecture.documents: Use a shared per-Xero-connection rate budget across imports, discovery and downloads. Honor provider remaining-limit headers and Retry-After. Deduplicate attachment-source discovery across cases and fan out metadata only to authorized linked cases. Queue newly linked or changed sources after import/linking; periodically recheck completed sources for newly added attachments. These capabilities are follow-up work, not implemented by the bounded-batch change.
targetArchitecture.freshnessTradeoff: Nightly automatic imports mean Xero changes can remain invisible until the next successful night. Explicit manual refresh remains available. Do not call the local view live Xero data.

rollout.action: User confirmed deployment on 2026-10-20. Query fixes, document worker, frontend and cron configuration were included in phase 1. Render schedule activation and duplicate-job checks are not independently verified.

Request-local timing traces now cover the complete Student Operations HTTP request and existing guard/workspace/query phases. Server-Timing and X-Correlation-ID headers plus CORS timing exposure allow browser and server measurements to join. Offline scripts/analyze-student-performance.mjs summarizes HAR and saved Runtime logs without exporting financial records or identity data. Collect authenticated samples after deploying this diagnostic change; compare sync-active/idle samples and independently verify hosting regions and plan/sleep behavior. Do not add caches or raise pool sizes without evidence.

Implement and integration-test a dependency-aware nightly invoice -> student reconciliation -> document pipeline with dedicated workers. Gate automatic creation to the Brisbane window; allow manual jobs at any time. Test UTC boundaries, retries, duplicate schedulers, restart recovery, missing scopes and disabled tenants before changing production schedules.

Confirm the Xero app tier and actual remaining daily allowance; add shared budget accounting, source deduplication, changed-source enqueueing and alerting before accelerating the historical document backlog.

roundTripFollowUp.source: Authenticated Server-Timing headers supplied by user on 2026-10-20
roundTripFollowUp.interpretation: Many separate database operations cost 179-196ms. Workspace work has four sequential statements; case links plus two filter-option statements add three more round trips after the register query. Pool acquisition includes connection creation and possible queueing; screenshots alone do not distinguish them. No sync-contention or p95 conclusion is drawn from these samples.
changes: Workspace resolution now uses two parameterized statements: resolve one active company/customer and set transaction-local tenant context, then read active entitlements and append exactly one allowed/denied audit event atomically. Tenant-scoped entitlement reads remain in a later statement so RLS cannot evaluate before context is set. Ambiguous/absent company bindings still fail closed.

Students keeps its main paginated query and combines case links, advisor choices and college choices into one aggregate metadata query. Four statements become two without changing role scope, sorting or filter contents.
Generic direct DatabaseService.query uses the existing batched BEGIN/SET LOCAL ROLE transaction helper. Effective runtime role and transaction cleanup are retained.

Idle client connections are retained for 60 seconds rather than the installed pg-pool default of 10 seconds. SOPHIA_RUNTIME_DB_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS can override this within 1-300 seconds. Maximum pool size is unchanged.
Timing headers and logs distinguish new/reused client acquisition and record total/idle/waiting counts before acquisition. The metadata and combined access-query durations have their own metrics.

infrastructure.databaseRegion: ap-southeast-2 (Sydney), confirmed from configured Neon connection hostname
infrastructure.renderRegions: Singapore, confirmed by user for both APIs and by the Runtime Render settings screenshot on 2026-10-20.
infrastructure.interpretation: Cross-region database access is confirmed and is a likely contributor to repeated 179-196ms operations. These samples do not isolate physical network latency from proxy, database or transaction overhead, or prove sync contention.
infrastructure.recommendation: Deploy the verified Runtime batching first and measure warm/new connections. Then evaluate colocating APIs and database. If non-Australian database residency is acceptable, a new Neon Singapore project is the least application-hosting change; if Australian residency is required, retain Sydney data and evaluate Sydney API hosting instead. Render currently does not list Sydney. Do not migrate production as part of this code deployment.
cutoverGates: Confirm data-residency requirements, all database consumers and explicit infrastructure migration approval before creating or copying production data.

Neon region is fixed per project: use a new project, not a branch. Rehearse a migration with the same PostgreSQL version; verify roles, grants, FORCE RLS, extensions, sequences and application behavior, not only row counts.

Plan backup, write quiescence or validated replication, pause all writers/schedulers during final cutover, update every consumer connection string, and validate invoice links, advisor reconciliation and document jobs before resuming. Retain the source without deleting it; rollback after target writes requires reconciliation, not a blind connection-string reversal.
Compare authenticated p50/p95 and pool-state metrics before and after. Same-region hosting reduces a source of latency but is not a guarantee of a particular page time.

roundTripFollowUp.deployment: Runtime deployment only; defaults activate batching and 60-second bounded idle reuse. Keep the timing flag enabled temporarily to compare warm/reused and new connections. No production writes or migration performed.

initialLoadFollowUp.source: User screenshots on 2026-10-20 plus frontend request-flow inspection
initialLoadFollowUp.interpretation: These are individual screenshot samples, not p95. Students workspace and list requests overlap. Payments workspace -> connection status -> invoices are sequential in the inspected code; each repeats login/access verification. Screenshots do not expose complete Server-Timing values and cannot establish the underlying database/identity breakdown.
changes: Students register response now includes the server-resolved workspace context; the page avoids its separate workspace request. Older responses fall back once to the legacy context endpoint.

New GET workspace/payments-register derives role, tenant and Trust connection server-side, returning initial invoice rows through one guard execution. It reuses existing local invoice query validation, sorting and pagination.
Payments displays initial rows before requesting optional sync freshness and payment-track choices. Later filters/pages use the existing fresh server-side invoice endpoint.

Operations/advisor roles keep their existing student view and cannot read integration data through the new endpoint. Missing or ambiguous connections retain existing behavior. Only a missing route (404), not an access failure, uses the legacy initial-load flow.
Initial queries respect restored pagination and filters. Filter changes during loading trigger a fresh invoice query without showing stale bootstrap rows or abandoning the workspace request.
Analyzer distinguishes payments-initial from later payments queries. No authorization or financial-record cache was added.
initialLoadFollowUp.deployment: Observed live in the user's subsequent screenshots: payments-register endpoint and Students response context are active. No migration or production data change.

implementation: SOPHIA_STUDENT_OPERATIONS_TIMING=1 enables middleware only for Student Operations routes. The default remains disabled.
AsyncLocalStorage isolates measurements across concurrent requests. Response content, authorization and tenant checks retain existing behavior.
Server-Timing includes app time, identity/access checks, workspace and list pool/setup/work/commit times and list query/options times when recorded. Nested phases overlap.
X-Correlation-ID joins the browser request, workspace guard, services and final HTTP log. Timing-Allow-Origin is restricted to configured CORS origins.
HTTP logs contain endpoint categories, status codes and durations, not raw URLs, student names, filters, credentials or response content.

The offline analyzer accepts HAR and/or saved Runtime logs, supports explicit sync-idle/sync-active labels, and reports p50/p95/max with sample counts. It performs no network requests or database access.

observedHealthChecks.origin: Local development machine, not the browser or Render internal network
observedHealthChecks.interpretation: Services responded successfully. These requests include database health checks, not authenticated page requests. First observed is not proof of a cold start; no p95 or hosting-region conclusion can be drawn from two samples.

captureProcedure: Deploy the updated Runtime; temporarily set SOPHIA_STUDENT_OPERATIONS_TIMING=1. No frontend deployment or database migration is required for phase 2 diagnostics.

In an authenticated browser session, preserve the Network log, load Students and Payments, and perform normal pagination/filter operations. Record at least 20 successful list requests per scenario. Keep page sizes consistent for comparisons.

Export the browser HAR locally and save Runtime logs covering that period. Record whether syncs were active or idle from actual job status. Do not deliberately start a production sync just to benchmark it.

From backend, run node scripts/analyze-student-performance.mjs --har /path/to/capture.har --logs /path/to/runtime.log --scenario sync-idle. Repeat with a separate observed sync-active sample. The command prints timing-only JSON.
Inspect browser waiting/transfer and server app/identity/workspace/pool/query metrics together. Do not add nested timings or equate browser outside-application time with pure network latency.
Check actual Render service region, database region, instance plan and restart/sleep logs in hosting configuration. Edge-network location does not prove the server region.
Disable the timing flag after collecting enough evidence. Use measured bottlenecks to choose the next optimization and worker deployment settings.
remainingEvidence: No authenticated browser session or hosting log connection is available in this workspace; no application token was generated or authentication bypassed for this audit.

Singapore APIs and Sydney Neon are confirmed. Authenticated full-page p95, slow identity requests, active-sync contention and cold starts remain unverified. Infrastructure relocation requires separate residency review and explicit approval.

capacity.limits: Xero documents 60 calls/minute and daily per-organisation limits of 1000 for Starter or 5000 for higher tiers. Tier was not verified for this deployment.
capacity.warning: 500 is a source budget per invocation, not a global provider-call quota: retries and other sync/download activity also consume calls. Do not run duplicate cron jobs or repeated manual batches without checking allowance.
capacity.backlog: The previously observed 6826 queued sources need at least 14 successful nights at 500/night, potentially longer with failures/time limits/new jobs. This change moves load overnight; it does not promise faster total backlog clearance than 25 hourly jobs. Increase throughput only after verifying tier/budget and adding source deduplication.

acceptanceAndMonitoring: Target warm authenticated list API p95 under 1 second and usable list within 2 seconds; these are proposed targets, not measured achievements.
Compare exact sorted rows, counts, filters and advisor role visibility before/after; verify no tenant leakage.
Record nightly job heartbeat, last success, queue age, processed/failed sources, retry-after and unresolved invoice count. Alert on a missed nightly run and growing backlog.
Run a controlled restart during a batch and confirm leases recover without duplicate case documents.
Rollback code/schedule independently if request latency or provider errors regress. Never reset queues, delete discovered documents or truncate local invoice data.
